prayerExcerpt.en-US: "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall find mercy."

meta.face: A Frank of about sixty with a fair, ruddy complexion and a LARGE, FULL, ROUND face — a broad forehead, FULL, heavy cheeks sagging into soft JOWLS and a DOUBLE CHIN, a SHORT, THICK, straight nose, deep-set, pale-blue eyes under HEAVY, DROOPING lids, red-rimmed as from weeping, thick fair-grey brows, a small, full mouth; LONG, fair-grey hair, parted in the middle and falling PAST THE SHOULDERS, the mark of the Merovingian kings; a drooping fair-grey MOUSTACHE and a short, rounded beard; the gaze compassionate and sorrowful, down toward the sick man.
meta.basis: No likeness from life; the gold tremissis struck at Chalon (Wikipedia's lead image) is a stylised profile. Wikipedia: the Merovingian kings wore their hair long, which set them apart from other Franks. Gregory of Tours (via Wikipedia) calls him caregiver to the sick, generous in plague and famine; the book says the same, and its engraving shows him among the sick. His burial in Saint-Marcel at Chalon is from Wikipedia. The heavy, full, jowled face is our choice.
